text:
The Maple Leafs had a lead in the second period and, for a few minutes, a way out of their homestand. Matt Boldy took it from them. His hat trick carried Minnesota to a 5-2 win in Toronto, the Leafs' fifth straight loss, all at home.

Boldy opened the scoring late in the first off a Kirill Kaprizov feed. Toronto turned it around early in the second: Auston Matthews tied it at 4:05 and Zack MacEwen, an undrafted forward playing just over 10 minutes, scored at 6:59 for a 2-1 lead that pushed the Leafs' win chance to 71%. It lasted under three minutes. Boldy tied it on a power-play slap shot, with Quinn Hughes and Kaprizov assisting, and then won it at 3:59 of the third, the night's biggest swing (48% to 75%). Michael McCarron and Danila Yurov, who had his first multi-point game of the season according to NHL.com's Heather Rule, added the rest.

Kaprizov had three assists and was on the ice for 3.07 expected goals for, the most of anyone. Minnesota also made the most of its chances in the third, out-chancing Toronto 2.64 to 1.23 in expected goals. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 28. Anthony Stolarz allowed 1.2 goals more than his 25 shots deserved. The overall game was closer than the score: we gave the Wild a 56% share of replays of every shot.

The Wild are a team on a run. Per Rule, they have won seven straight on the road, outscoring teams 28-10, and extended their point streak to 10 games. They are also a team with questions, and Hughes's contract stalemate dominates their coverage. On this night he played 28:30 and assisted on the tying goal.

Toronto's slide has a lot of storylines attached. William Nylander, in a TSN headline, insisted his form is "not that slumpy", the rookie Gavin McKenna's growing pains are getting heavy coverage, and Matthews has been in the headlines for calling out his teammates after the loss to New Jersey. A homestand that was supposed to steady things has done the opposite.
headline: Boldy's hat trick sinks Leafs, Wild keep rolling
